subject: Meaning of loo in sem and cfa models via blavaan

messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: Meaning of loo in sem and cfa models via blavaan
parts:
Hi all,

When using the loo statistic via Stan or loo it is typically calculated on a single outcome variable.  However, one can calculate the loo in blavaan using blavCompare and get a single number or loo difference if comparing two models.  In a CFA model or SEM model with multiple endogenous variables, how is the single loo value being calculated?

Also, is it true that specifying "extra_code" can only be handled using JAGS?

Thanks

David

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Meaning of loo in sem and cfa models via blavaan
parts:
Hi David,

The loo statistic is based on the model log-likelihood, which can be viewed as scoring the models' predictions of observed data. I have a Psychometrika paper describing related details, preprint is here:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04452

About the extra code: I think JAGS is the best bet for using the mcmcextra route. For target="stan", you have to export the Stan file via mcmcfile = TRUE and then edit that Stan file yourself. But the Stan model is pretty big and not necessarily intuitive (it is intended to handle most models that the user would request, so has to be big).

Ed

Thanks for the quick response, Ed.  I'll read over the paper.  I've used the LOO to compute the expected log-predictive score for each left out observation on some focal outcome of interest.  In a path model there are mediators and outcomes, so one has a system of equations.  I wasn't sure how loo was calculated in that case.

Best

David
